newsitem.title: UK: Dixons shares rebound from recent decline.
newsitem.headline: Dixons shares rebound from recent decline.

text.p: Shares in electrical retailer Dixons Group Plc rose on Wednesday, rebounding from recent weakness inspired in part by the sale of shares by chairman Sir Stanley Kalms, dealers said.
"It fell seven percent on Monday and every stock eventually has a bit of a bounce," said one market-maker.
Dixons shares were up 9p at 491-1/2 by 1113 GMT, after on Tuesday touching their lowest level in some six months.
Dealers said analysts at HSBC James Capel said yesterday the stock was looking cheap after its recent tumble, though analysts at Capel were not immediately available for comment.

Market sources said analysts at Merrill Lynch on Monday cut the stock to "reduce" from "neutral," arguing that recent growth in personal computers and related products -- which account for 26 percent of Dixons sales -- was unsustainable.
Analysts at Merrill were not immediately available for comment.
